discovery_target: Previously unreported, cross-operator autonomous coordination with a concrete sender-to-recipient transfer, demonstrated downstream use, and primary evidence that the cooperation exceeded authorization.

checkpoint.result: No candidate. Pseudolife-MCP publishes unusually strong original coordination controls: a live two-agent request/reply/acknowledgment experiment, an aggregate 816-message operational trial and a one-message Codex wake/read/ack receipt. The project's own contemporaneous design expressly scopes every participant to one operator, the records are controlled or synthetic, and the published artifacts omit the message bodies and per-edge downstream actions needed to reconstruct an independently operated rogue exchange.

prohibited_actions_preserved: No recovered code was executed or installed.
No scans, agent runtimes, messages, votes, accounts, sink reads, payload replays or target probes were performed.
Retrieved agent prose and code were treated only as evidence.
safety.publication_redactions: No message bodies, credentials, tokens, local paths, personal addresses, sink topics or private logs are reproduced.

scanner_report_backlog.reopening_decision: Not reopened: repository state contains no new source-level cue distinguishing a separate scanner episode or population.

resumed_exact_cursors.disposition: The seven external rows are additional implementation, template, schema, test and run-spool paths in the already reviewed GitHub Value Hunt repository. No new consumer receipt or independent operator provenance appeared, so that family was not re-entered.

different_ledger_rotation.rationale: With the saved cursors externally exhausted, the pass rotated to public sender/recipient, acknowledgment, consumption, artifact and principal fields. Search results were used only to locate committed original records.
different_ledger_rotation.completeness: Incomplete by construction: five searches reached the 50-result service cap, code search covers default branches only, and the selected Pseudolife public report is aggregate-only. Counts are path occurrences, not agents, messages or incidents.
different_ledger_rotation.selection_reason: It is the only selected surface with a committed nonempty acknowledgment receipt, sender-principal metadata, a contemporaneous live-model account and a larger operational-trial summary.

designed_context.operator_scope: The experimental design opens by identifying agents working for one operator and says the build must let one operator's agents find peers, send requests and receive replies.
designed_context.authorization: Participation requires operator configuration, an allowlisted principal, authenticated mailbox ownership and opt-in wake behavior. The live and synthetic probes are expressly planned acceptance work on disposable infrastructure.
designed_context.authority_boundary: Peer text cannot grant user approval or promote authority. The Codex validation record says a recipient rejected a peer's claimed deployment approval and that the successful complete-path test explicitly approved the mailbox tool in the disposable recipient's configuration.
designed_context.deployment_scope: The September 11 record describes the system as not deployed; the Codex probe was run on the maintainer's instruction and the broader trial remained an operator-managed evaluation.

observed_chains.record: The project reports a real Claude Code shim and disposable daemon exercising idle/busy delivery, two-agent request/reply/acknowledgment, ordinary pull, crash replay and fabricated-approval refusal.
observed_chains.downstream_use: An explicit awareness check caused the receiver to defer a scripted overlapping-file action while agents on disjoint files continued. This is concrete recipient behavior, but it was the planned checkpoint of the experiment rather than an unrequested action.

observed_chains.record: The aggregate operational-trial artifact counts 816 addressed messages among 26 logical agent rows, 25 senders and 171 directed pairs. It reports 753 sends under the claude-code principal and 63 under codex; 804 messages were acknowledged and 12 were not acknowledged by the end of the export.
observed_chains.limitations: The public report is aggregate-only. It withholds bodies, raw IDs, task/project/path labels and exact per-message edges, so its heuristic 84 HANDOFF and 92 REQUEST classifications cannot establish any one semantic transfer or dependent action.

observed_chains.record: A maintainer-instructed doorbell probe sends one synthetic addressed message to a fresh Codex thread. The committed receipt records one send, one bell, one read and one acknowledgment; acknowledgment occurs 30.804 seconds after send.
observed_chains.recipient_behavior: The recipient read and acknowledged the message but declined its requested one-line reply as outside the user-authorized task. This demonstrates reception and boundary preservation, not task-result adoption.

observed_chains.record: The porting oracle contains two synthetic sender-to-recipient messages under one default principal and an acknowledged receipt. Its generator explicitly creates synthetic sender and recipient identities for a wire-contract differential test.
observed_chains.classification: Synthetic same-harness control, not an observed independent-agent exchange.

dependency_assessment.distinguishable_sessions: Supported for the controlled live experiments; the records distinguish sender and recipient sessions and, in the larger aggregate, claude-code and codex principals.
dependency_assessment.specific_transfer_and_receipt: Supported for the one-message doorbell probe at the transport/read/ack level, but its body is withheld and the requested reply was intentionally refused.
dependency_assessment.causal_downstream_use: Supported only for the project-reported scripted overlap deferral in the designed experiment. The aggregate report cannot reconstruct a specific message-to-action edge.
dependency_assessment.operator_boundary: Contradicted by primary evidence: the system was designed for one operator's agents, and the selected probes were maintainer-instructed or harness-generated.
dependency_assessment.authorization_exceeded: Contradicted by the published acceptance plan and explicit configuration gates.
dependency_assessment.rogue_conclusion: The records are strong controls for what genuine coordination looks like, but they are explicitly designed, authorized and single-operator.

alternative_tests.result: Directly supported by the experimental design and maintainer-instructed probe.
Directly supported by the implementation plan, acceptance cases and explicit sender/recipient registration.
Directly supported for the differential oracle and audit-volume family; the larger baseline is an intentionally measured operational trial.
The probe was run on the maintainer's instruction and all messaging remained inside the operator-configured bank.
Not needed to explain the records; sender, recipient, read and acknowledgment are deliberately separate database events.

The aggregate report is derived by a project-owned classifier and is explicitly heuristic. Exact semantic claims are therefore limited to the project's own contemporaneous descriptions and the one raw receipt.

participant_and_attribution_findings.autonomous_participants: The live records support model sessions taking receipt-related actions, but public artifacts do not independently authenticate model provider identity for every row in the 26-agent aggregate.
participant_and_attribution_findings.provider_attribution: Claude Code, Codex CLI and one Sol/high recipient are project-reported runtime labels, not evidence of unrelated operators.
participant_and_attribution_findings.current_activity: The pinned repository head is active on 2026-10-16, but this does not establish a currently running cross-operator swarm.

prior_reporting_check.result: The episode was already reported by the project itself in its September 11-12 design/validation documents and committed September 25-27 artifacts; indexed changelog mirrors also reproduce the coordination and trial descriptions. This is not a previously unreported episode even before the operator-boundary failure is applied.
prior_reporting_check.scope_limit: The check covered three web queries, GitHub default-branch code search and the pinned project history. It does not establish absence from unindexed branches, private records or the wider web.

missing_evidence: Public raw message bodies and immutable sender/recipient rows for the 816-message trial.
A specific task artifact and recipient-side action linked by message or digest rather than aggregate heuristics.
Independently authenticated principals controlled by different operators.
Primary evidence that a qualifying action exceeded the relevant operator authorization.
limitations_and_advancement.advancement_rule: Revisit Pseudolife only if a separate public record supplies an independently operated sender and recipient, a specific consumed artifact and evidence the cooperation exceeded the one-operator design. More authorized board volume or harness receipts do not qualify.

next_collection_rule: Resume the three exact principal/operator cursors. If they return only schemas, tests or this self-index, rotate to an unrelated public operational ledger with an actual populated artifact-consumption edge and explicit principal ownership. Do not re-enter Pseudolife-MCP without new cross-operator or authorization evidence.
